errors.text: The central mechanism is inverted relative to the target: the hypothesis treats lattice-distortion-mediated sluggish diffusion as the principal stability control, whereas the target finds active, non-sluggish diffusion governed by surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation.
The proposed material and treatment do not reconstruct the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, PLD initial state, vacuum ramp heating, or stepped in situ STEM protocol.
The comparative experiment changes elemental chemistry, size mismatch, mixing enthalpy, melting points, and surface energies simultaneously, so it cannot isolate local lattice distortion.

The claim that high size mismatch plus negative mixing enthalpy should preserve a single phase is not generally valid; strongly negative pair enthalpies can instead favor ordered intermetallic formation.

Stability of the nominally low-distortion set would not establish that configurational entropy alone caused stability, because surface energetics, kinetic trapping, phase thermodynamics, and synthesis history remain uncontrolled.
